Tell us your town and what your station charges.

posts.claim: The government has banned media houses from livestreaming 2027 election results.
posts.truth: No ban on livestreaming election results exists in Kenyan law today.
proof: President William Ruto dismissed claims of any plan to stop live tallies.
Article 34 of the Constitution protects media freedom and public broadcast rights.
Former CS Justin Muturi asked the IEBC to issue binding coverage rules.
posts.pride: Kenyan elections depend on open scrutiny and constitutional safeguards.
posts.message: No ban exists on livestreaming 2027 election results. Media freedom is constitutionally protected.
posts.action: Track election reforms and regulations directly on the official portal at iebc.or.ke
beats: Reports claiming a *livestream ban* on 2027 election results are false.
President William Ruto confirmed the government plans no media restrictions.
The Constitution protects the right of broadcasters to cover public tallies.
Kenyans demand: the IEBC gazettes clear *livestreaming rules* well before 2027.
posts.caption:
Claims of a state ban on livestreaming 2027 election results are false. The Constitution protects media coverage and open tallying of votes.

What rules do you want the IEBC to put in place for 2027?

#SetItStraight #KenyaOnRecord
posts.impact: Assures voters that 2027 presidential poll results remain open to public media scrutiny.

scripts.radio:
Good evening. This is Kenya on Record, bringing you the facts that shape our public life and economy.

First, on energy infrastructure: the Garissa Solar Power Plant is now delivering 54.65 megawatts of clean power into the national grid. Harnessing solar potential in northern Kenya is a necessary step toward diversifying our energy mix. The accountability question remains whether these clean megawatts will translate into lower, more predictable electricity tariffs for Kenyan households and businesses.

Second, on public assets: a critical national debate has opened up over whether the government should sell a 25 percent stake in the Kenya Pipeline Company to the Dangote Group. Kenya Pipeline is a profitable, strategic national utility that underpins fuel distribution across the region. As citizens, we must ask: does private capital improve efficiency, or does divesting critical infrastructure compromise our energy sovereignty? Public participation on this transaction must be genuine and transparent.

Finally, a vital health advisory: salt water does not cure or prevent Ebola. Drinking or bathing in high concentrations of salt water is dangerous and offers zero protection. Rely strictly on certified health guidelines and report any symptoms immediately to authorized medical facilities.

Kwa ufupi: Mtambo wa sola wa Garissa unaingiza megawati 54.65 kwenye gridi ya taifa. Wananchi wanajadili mpango wa serikali kuuza asilimia 25 ya hisa za Kenya Pipeline kwa kampuni ya Dangote. Na ukweli wa afya: maji ya chumvi hayatibu Ebola; fuata ushauri wa wataalamu wa afya pekee. 

Stay informed, and hold the record.
scripts.voice_note:
Habari zenu. Here is your weekly accountability update from Kenya on Record.

First, a critical health warning: salt water does not cure or prevent Ebola. Please disregard those viral messages. Rely strictly on verified health ministry guidelines, and report suspected symptoms to a hospital immediately.

On the national balance sheet, a major debate is brewing: should the government sell a 25 percent stake in Kenya Pipeline to Dangote? KPC is a profitable strategic asset handling our regional fuel corridor. We need total transparency on valuation and terms before public property is signed away.

On energy, Garissa Solar Plant is feeding 54.65 megawatts of renewable power into the national grid. The real test is whether our power bills reflect that clean energy.

Forward this note to your groups to keep the facts straight.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Maji ya chumvi haitibu Ebola. Beware of fake health remedies online. If unwell, seek immediate medical care from certified facilities.
scripts.reels:
Should Kenya sell a 25 percent stake in Kenya Pipeline to the Dangote Group?

KPC is not a struggling parastatal. It is a profitable, strategic artery that secures fuel supply across East Africa.

Private capital can drive expansion, but selling public monopolies requires total transparency, not closed-door deals.

Is this a smart strategic partnership, or the surrender of a vital national asset? Put your voice on record.
